what_its_for: Abemaciclib is a cancer medicine used to treat certain types of breast cancer in adults. It is used for hormone receptor-positive (HR+), HER2-negative breast cancer. It may be used alone or combined with other medicines like hormonal therapy (such as fulvestrant or an aromatase inhibitor) to help slow or stop cancer growth. It works by blocking proteins that help cancer cells grow and divide.
how_to_take: Take abemaciclib by mouth (swallow whole) with or without food, two times a day (every 12 hours). Try to take it at the same times each day. Do not crush, chew, or split the tablets. If you vomit after taking a dose, do NOT take an extra dose — just take your next scheduled dose at the regular time.
dosing: The usual dose is 150 mg taken twice daily when used in combination with hormonal therapy, or 200 mg taken twice daily when used alone. Your doctor may lower your dose if you have side effects. Always follow your doctor's specific dosing instructions — do not change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, skip it and take your next dose at the regularly scheduled time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed dose. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store abemaciclib tablets at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep tablets in the original container, away from moisture, heat, and light. Keep this medicine out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit, grapefruit juice, and Seville oranges (bitter oranges) while taking this medicine, as they can increase the amount of drug in your body and worsen side effects. Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and herbal supplements you take, especially drugs like rifampin, ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, or St. John's Wort, as they can interact with abemaciclib. Avoid becoming pregnant while taking this medicine — use effective birth control during treatment and for at least 3 weeks after your last dose.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe or frequent diarrhea (especially watery or bloody), signs of infection (fever over 100.4°F, chills, cough, painful urination), unusual bruising or bleeding, shortness of breath or chest pain (possible blood clot signs), severe nausea or vomiting that prevents you from eating or drinking, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), or dark urine. Also contact your doctor if you notice any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Abemaciclib starts working right away at a cellular level, but you may not feel the effects immediately. Your doctor will monitor your response through regular lab tests and imaging. Most people begin to see benefits over weeks to months of treatment. It is very important to keep taking this medicine as prescribed, even if you feel well, unless your doctor tells you to stop.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Do NOT use abemaciclib if you are pregnant — it can harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant must use effective birth control. Do not breastfeed while taking this medicine and for at least 3 weeks after the last dose. Kidney or liver problems: Your doctor may need to adjust your dose if you have moderate to severe kidney or liver disease — always tell your doctor about any organ problems. Older adults (65+): This medicine can be used in older adults, but side effects like diarrhea and low blood cell counts may be more likely; your doctor will monitor you closely.
